summary: Self-hosted gateway that gives you one OpenAI-style API for many model providers, with keys, quotas and load balancing.

heroCommands.command: docker run --name one-api -d --restart always -p 3000:3000 -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai -v /home/ubuntu/data/one-api:/data justsong/one-api

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: One API is an LLM API management and distribution system. It lets you reach many large models (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek and more) through the standard OpenAI API format, and manages tokens, quotas, users and channels.
sixtySeconds.problem: Each AI provider has its own API and keys. One API puts them behind one endpoint so apps only speak the OpenAI format, while you control who can use what.
whoFor: Developers who want one API for many providers
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a widely used, MIT-licensed gateway with load balancing across channels, streaming, token and quota management, and a simple Docker deploy.
requirements: MySQL recommended for high concurrency (SQLite by default)

overview: Run the Docker image (SQLite by default; add SQL_DSN for MySQL). Data and logs go to the host folder you mount. Then open http://localhost:3000.
The initial login is root with password 123456, which you should change immediately.

Features include load balancing across channels, stream mode, multi-machine deployment, token expiry and usage limits, user and channel groups with different rates, quota details and announcements. The project is MIT licensed.
limitations: Default admin password must be changed
Follow each provider's terms when sharing access
